quote.quote: A meeting of the Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) was held on January 29, 2013, to discuss this application.

**January 29, 2013:** NDA was discussed at a Pulmonary Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) meeting. The PADAC voted 15 to 1 favoring approval as there was adequate clinical evidence of safety/efficacy.

recommendation.text: The committee voted favorably on all questions: substantial evidence of efficacy (15 yes, 1 no, 1 abstain), safety of olodaterol (15 yes, 1 no, 1 abstain), and approvability (15 yes, 1 no, 1 abstain) — i.e., in favor of approval.

quote.quote: Regarding the approvability question, which is essentially the sum of the demonstration of efficacy and safety, the results were in favor of approval (15 yes, 1 no, and 1 abstain).

summary: The Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) met on January 29, 2013 and voted 15 yes, 1 no, 1 abstain on each of three questions — substantial evidence of efficacy, acceptable safety, and approvability — endorsing approval of olodaterol (Striverdi Respimat) 5 mcg once daily for COPD. The review documents describe this as an essentially favorable meeting; the committee's only noted safety observation (4 small cell lung carcinoma cases, all in the 10 mcg arm, which members felt may have been random and warranting post-marketing surveillance) and its discussion of the unsupported exercise-endurance claim are not explicitly tied in the reviews to any resulting change in the approval (no PMR/PMC for the neoplasm signal appears in the approval letter, and the reviews attribute disallowing the exercise claim to the clinical review's own assessment). Approval was ultimately delayed by a Complete Response for manufacturing/GMP deficiencies unrelated to the AdCom, so no supported concern-to-change linkage could be established.
